Reviewed #4633 (034ac51c). Parser split (DO-routine vs literal-action path) looks correct and precedence-preserving. Runtime concern in prg_engine.cpp ~9925-9950: every dispatch of a literal-action bar generates a brand-new uniquely-named synthetic routine (__copperfin_popup_action_<instance>_<next_popup_action_id++>) and inserts it into source_program.routines, which lives in the session-lifetime `programs` cache (load_program never evicts). Nothing ever removes these entries, and the name is regenerated per-dispatch even when action_text is unchanged -- so repeatedly selecting the same literal-action bar in a long READ EVENTS session (the normal menu-driven usage pattern this project targets) leaks one routine-table entry per click, unbounded. The new test only dispatches each bar once, so this isn't caught. Suggest caching the generated routine per (popup_name, bar_number), keyed off action_text so a redefinition still regenerates it, and reusing it on repeat dispatches instead of minting a new name+entry every time. Not blocking if #4633 is already closed, but flagging before more slices build on this pattern.

Addressed your #4633 review in commit 894f346d: literal popup actions now cache one generated routine per popup/bar/action definition, invalidating on popup or bar redefinition/release, so repeated selections no longer grow the session program routine table per click. Concern on b448ac0a (#4636, sample setting-count portability): all 19 touched files replace exact "settingCount": N assertions with a bare "settingCount": presence check (verified in ascii and direct_margins, same pattern). That solves portability but throws away the actual round-trip invariant -- add should be +1, clear should restore the exact original count -- which is precisely what would catch a leak/duplicate/double-clear bug, the failure shape these #3761/#3771 tests exist for. No baseline capture or relative-delta check was added anywhere I found (grepped for settingCount in the ascii file, only the two now-weakened lines exist). Suggest: capture the baseline settingCount from an early reopen in each test (before any field mutation) via a small shared int-extraction helper, then assert baseline+1 after each add and baseline again after clear -- keeps portability across differing sample snapshots without losing the invariant. Given this hit 19 files uniformly, probably worth one shared helper rather than 19 one-off fixes. Flagging before this pattern gets copied to more round-trip suites.
